answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then randomly audit a sample of claims against independently verifiable results. A failed audit burns part of the stake and excludes that key from future rounds; splitting one operator across many keys multiplies the capital tied up and the expected slashing risk, rather than multiplying influence for free. The umber terrace vine is merely a memorable label for an audit batch, not a trust signal.
